# Other Commands

### maxdata &lt;megabytes&gt; { #maxdata .command data-toc-label="maxdata" }

Sets the room for the data files your mod's Lua script saves. Goes in the .c5se or on a `#!@` line, once.

- **megabytes:** The room your script's data files may take, 1 to 100. Without the line, 10. A save that would go past it fails, and CoE5SE deletes nothing to make room.

=== ".c5se"

    ```c5se
    maxdata 20
    ```

=== ".c5m"

    ```c5m
    #!@maxdata 20
    ```

### include "&lt;file&gt;" <span class="new-badge">New</span> { #include .command data-toc-label="include" }

Lets you arrange your mod in as many .c5se files and folders as you wish, for your own organization: by faction, by region, or by units, spells, and events. Put the `include` lines only in your mod's ROOT files: [its .c5se](index.md), or `#!@` lines of its .c5m.

```text
LOTROverhaulMod/
├── LOTROverhaulMod.c5m     ◀── ROOT: include lines go here
├── LOTROverhaulMod.c5se    ◀── ROOT: include lines go here
├── ring_quest.c5se         ◀── included: no include lines
└── rohan/
    └── riders.c5se         ◀── included: no include lines
```

- **file:** The path from the folder that holds your .c5m, with `/` between folders, ending in `.c5se`. Any number of folders deep. Letters, digits, `_`, `-` and `.` only, no folder or file name starting with a dot (so no `..`), capitals as on disk.

Write anything in those files you'd write in your .c5se, events and [settings](mod-settings.md) included.

The game reads your mod top to bottom, each included file at its `include` line.

Edits take effect the next time the game reads the mods, such as leaving the Mods screen or loading a game, with no restart.

Keep each block, such as a `newmonster` or an event, inside one file. An event still open at a file's end stops the game with "Missing endevent".

Ship the folders with your mod. In a network or hotseat game, changing a file after the game started ends the game.

Including a missing file, or one twice, stops the game with the Mod Error. An `include` inside an event, an included file, or a .c5m line without `#!@` does too. For a mistake inside an included file, the Mod Error gives its path and line.

=== ".c5se"

    ```c5se
    include "rohan/riders.c5se"
    include "mordor/orcs.c5se"
    ```

=== ".c5m"

    ```c5m
    #!@include "rohan/riders.c5se"
    #!@include "mordor/orcs.c5se"
    ```

```c5se title="rohan/riders.c5se"
# Rohan's riders and their spell
newmonster "Rider of Rohan"
copystats "Knight"
copyspr "Knight"

newmonster "Marshal of the Mark"
copystats "Knight"
copyspr "Knight"

newspell "Leechcraft of the Mark"
path "White Magic"
level 1
weapon 4 "Heal"
```

### selectclass "&lt;class&gt;" <span class="new-badge">New</span> { #selectclass .command data-toc-label="selectclass" }

Picks a class by string, as a mod's class number changes with the mods a player has on, since CoE5SE gives mods 50 more class slots.

- **class:** The class's name in double quotes, as `setclassname` gave it, capitals included. When two classes share a name, the game's class comes first, then the earliest mod's.

A name no class has stops the game with its Mod Error at that line, naming the class. Turn on the mod with the class, and make it load before yours.

=== ".c5se"

    ```c5se
    selectclass "Stewards of Gondor"
    ```

=== ".c5m"

    ```c5m
    #!@selectclass "Stewards of Gondor"
    ```

### aiclass 2 <span class="new-badge">New</span> { #aiclass .command data-toc-label="aiclass" }

Takes the class away from every player, human and AI: Choose Class leaves it out, and no Random player gets it. Goes after `newclass` or `selectclass`. Clear the game's classes out of a total rework with it, so no Baron or Senator turns up in Middle-earth.

Leave enough classes for every Random player. With "unique random players" on and more AIs than classes left to them, the extra AIs get your `aiclass 2` classes. The game can't start a Random player with no class to pick.

=== ".c5se"

    ```c5se
    aiclass 2
    ```

=== ".c5m"

    ```c5m
    aiclass 2
    ```

!!! tip "For players without CoE5SE"
    Their game reads `aiclass 2` as `aiclass 1`: only AI players get the class.

!!! info "More in the game's manual"
    `aiclass` and the game's other class commands are in Illwinter's official modding manual, under ["Class Modding"](https://www.illwinter.com/coe5/coe5modding.pdf#page=27).

### Example { #example }

=== ".c5se"

    ```c5se
    maxdata 20
    include "ring_quest.c5se"
    include "rohan/riders.c5se"
    include "rohan/edoras/spells.c5se"
    include "gondor/minas_tirith/guard.c5se"
    include "mordor/orcs.c5se"
    include "mordor/barad_dur/rituals.c5se"

    selectclass "Baron"
    aiclass 2
    selectclass "Senator"
    aiclass 2
    selectclass "Monkey Maharaja"
    aiclass 2
    ```

=== ".c5m"

    ```c5m
    #!@maxdata 20
    #!@include "ring_quest.c5se"
    #!@include "rohan/riders.c5se"
    #!@include "rohan/edoras/spells.c5se"
    #!@include "gondor/minas_tirith/guard.c5se"
    #!@include "mordor/orcs.c5se"
    #!@include "mordor/barad_dur/rituals.c5se"

    #!@selectclass "Baron"
    aiclass 2
    #!@selectclass "Senator"
    aiclass 2
    #!@selectclass "Monkey Maharaja"
    aiclass 2
    ```

Your mod's folder with those files:

```text
LOTROverhaulMod/
├── LOTROverhaulMod.c5m     ◀── ROOT: include lines go here
├── LOTROverhaulMod.c5se    ◀── ROOT: include lines go here
├── ring_quest.c5se
├── rohan/
│   ├── riders.c5se
│   └── edoras/
│       └── spells.c5se
├── gondor/
│   └── minas_tirith/
│       └── guard.c5se
└── mordor/
    ├── orcs.c5se
    └── barad_dur/
        └── rituals.c5se
```
